newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent diesel differentials steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent diesel differentials steady.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot low sulphur diesel differentials were steady late Friday after easing in Chicago early in the day, traders said.

Discussion remained relatively quiet as several players were out of the market following the midweek New Year's Day holiday, and the pace of trading activity was expected to pick up again on Monday, traders said.
"The holidays are over. Things should be back to normal on Monday," one Chicago-area trader said.

Low sulphur diesel for January deliveries was bid 5.25 cents a gallon under NYMEX February heating oil in both Chicago and Group Three in a day that saw front-month heating oil futures close down more than 0.75 cent a gallon.
High sulphur diesel for January deliveries remained 6.0 cents a gallon under the print in Chicago and 7.50 cents under the print in Group Three, traders said.
Unleaded gasoline was steady at 2.75/2.50 cents a gallon under NYMEX February unleaded for January deliveries in Chicago and Group Three, where later deliveries were 0.25 cent a gallon stronger.
Jet/kero was bid 1.25 cent a gallon over the print in Chicago on strong demand, and was talked 4.25/4.0 cents a gallon under the print in Group Three, traders said.
